title: Transformations in height; local Swiss reference frames; REFRAME geoservices
identifier: Official swisstopo technical guidance for LV95, LN02, LHN95 and height transformations
access_status: Public official technical guidance; linked for technical reference
review_note: Reviewed swisstopo's official pages on height transformations, local Swiss reference frames and REFRAME geoservices. LV95 is the official horizontal reference frame; LN02 remains the official Swiss height reference. LHN95 is a distinct orthometric height system. Swisstopo states that an exact LN02–LHN95 transformation is not possible because the systems differ in nature and LN02 contains distortions; approximate transformations may be decimetric. REFRAME supports transformations involving LV95, LN02, LHN95 and ellipsoidal heights, but correct input-frame identification remains the operator's responsibility.
cautions: Do not treat EPSG:2056 alone as a complete statement of the vertical reference of a 3D coordinate.
Do not claim exact or centimetric equivalence between LN02 and LHN95; swisstopo states exact transformation is not possible and approximations can be decimetric.
Transformation quality depends on correct input frame identification and the applicable transformation method.
Use the current official transformation service and retain original coordinates, input/output frame labels, transformation method and date.

title: Model Diagnostics and Forecast Evaluation for Quantiles
identifier: Annual Review of Statistics and Its Application, 10, 597–621; DOI 10.1146/annurev-statistics-032921-020240
access_status: Open access article under CC BY 4.0 according to publisher record
review_note: Inspected the review abstract and accessible article material on in-sample model diagnostics versus out-of-sample forecast evaluation, unconditional and conditional calibration, quantile reliability diagrams and consistent scoring functions. Used to frame calibration and sharpness as distinct aspects of predictive performance.
cautions: The review focuses on quantile forecasts and related probabilistic prediction settings; not every result transfers unchanged to every spatial model.
Calibration and sharpness must be assessed relative to the forecast target and evaluation design.
Aggregated calibration can conceal conditional or spatial miscalibration.

title: Geospatial View of the Generic Statistical Business Process Model (GeoGSBPM)
access_status: Open access; Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 IGO stated in publication
review_note: Inspected the official PDF, including its framing of geospatially enabled statistics, integration of geography across the statistical production process, and phase structure covering needs specification, design, build, collect, process, analyse, disseminate and evaluate. Used as a lifecycle reference for the learning pathway.
cautions: Framework is designed for official-statistics production and is not a study-specific sampling or inference prescription.
Adaptation is required for individual research, operational, commercial and field projects.
The framework does not replace statistical, geodetic, measurement or domain expertise.

title: Geospatial Analysis Work Flow Overview
identifier: Geospatial Analysis for Optimization at Environmental Sites
access_status: Public web guidance
review_note: Inspected the official workflow page describing project goals and data requirements, exploratory analysis, method selection, model building, cross-validation and validation, result generation and use in optimization. Used as an applied spatial-analysis workflow example.
cautions: The guidance is grounded in environmental-site and optimization contexts; it is not a universal workflow standard or a substitute for domain-specific methods.
Statements about method performance should be interpreted in context and not generalized to every spatial problem.
Validation and uncertainty procedures must be selected for the target estimand and deployment task.

issuer: Olofsson, Pontus; Foody, Giles M.; Herold, Martin; Stehman, Stephen V.; Woodcock, Curtis E.; Wulder, Michael A.
title: Good practices for estimating area and assessing accuracy of land change
jurisdiction: International remote sensing and land-change assessment
access_status: Publisher abstract and accessible repository copy inspected
review_note: Inspected the article abstract and accessible full-text copy. Reviewed its sampling, response and analysis framework; probability sampling recommendations; area-proportion error matrix; overall, user's and producer's accuracy; reference-class area estimation; uncertainty intervals; and documentation of reference-label and protocol limitations. Used as the principal methodological source for the bounded mapped-class-stratified estimator.
cautions: The article presents design-dependent estimators; formulas must not be transferred to a different sampling design without justification.
The accompanying repository implementation covers only independent simple random sampling within mapped-class strata.
Reference-label uncertainty, nonresponse and uncertainty in mapped-area weights require additional treatment.
A probability sample and suitable response protocol are prerequisites for design-based population inference.

issuer: John Duncan; Pacific Data Hub / Pacific Community
title: Fiji Land Use Land Cover Test Dataset
identifier: Pacific Data Hub dataset ID 8c08f0c0-eb8e-4a74-83b4-58d1598d95de; GeoJSON resource 3be50a34-8292-4886-9ed3-1488d6ae08f1
access_status: Public GeoJSON available through Pacific Data Hub and the author's GitHub repository; ODbL
review_note: Inspected the dataset description and README and parsed the pinned GeoJSON at repository revision 050021d57c99abaaa6f2c511e4f718a402c7ca2a. The file contains 834 point features with unique coordinates, seven mapped-class strata of 100 points each and 134 tree-stratum points. The source text states 834 total points but describes 133 tree points, an allocation arithmetic discrepancy (100*7+133=833). The published eligible stratum pixel counts sum to 157,057,276. The sample was selected by stratified random sampling within 2021 mapped classes and visually labelled using 2021 Sentinel-2, Planet NICFI and Google Satellite imagery. The eligible frame excludes Tikinas used for training. The case analysis maps strata to the original 2021 map classes and uses the supplied pixel counts as stratum population sizes; it does not independently reconstruct the raster, training exclusion mask or reference interpretations.
cautions: ODbL applies; check attribution and share-alike obligations before redistributing the database or substantial adapted contents.

The 2021 sample strata are the mapped classes of the Fiji map used to define the sample. Applying the sample to another map requires extracting that map's classes and an estimator supporting strata different from map classes.
The sample frame and supplied stratum pixel counts exclude Tikinas used for training; estimates do not automatically represent every pixel in Fiji.
The source documentation says 133 tree-stratum samples while the pinned GeoJSON contains 134; the discrepancy must be reported, not silently reconciled.
Reference labels are quality-checked visual interpretations, not field observations independently re-verified in this repository.
The supplied stratum pixel counts and map-area weights were accepted from the dataset documentation and were not independently reconstructed from the source raster.
The sample is not a probability sample of every pixel in the full national extent where training Tikinas were excluded.

title: ESA WorldCover 2021 v200 Product User Manual
access_status: Public PDF
review_note: Inspected the official WorldCover 2021 v200 product manual for product purpose, 10 m mapping, Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 inputs, product legend and known limitations. The manual distinguishes the 2020 v100 and 2021 v200 algorithm versions and cautions against interpreting differences between those products as pure land-cover change. Also inspected the manual's 3° × 3° tile scheme, EPSG:4326 delivery, and filename convention encoding the lower-left tile coordinate; used these details to derive and audit the five Fiji COG source URLs.
cautions: The product's global accuracy figures are not local accuracy estimates for Fiji.
WorldCover 2020 v100 and 2021 v200 use different algorithm versions; map differences combine algorithm and land-cover changes.
A class crosswalk to another legend is an analyst decision and requires explicit documentation.

issuer: European Space Agency / ESA WorldCover Consortium
title: ESA WorldCover data access, product versions and licence
access_status: Public web documentation
review_note: Inspected official product access documentation. Confirms WorldCover 2021 v200, the 11-class product, 10 m Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF tiles in EPSG:4326, tile delivery, download mechanisms, CC BY 4.0 terms and required attribution. It explicitly says WMS/WMTS are for display and not suitable for analytical extraction because they are represented as RGB imagery.
cautions: Use analytical raster map layers rather than rendered WMS/WMTS imagery for class extraction.
Record the exact tile versions and source fingerprints used in an analysis.
Required product attribution and citation should accompany redistributed outputs.

issuer: ESA WorldCover Consortium; Wageningen University; IIASA
title: WorldCover Product Validation Report v2.0
identifier: ESA WorldCover 2021 v200 Product Validation Report, Version 2.0
access_status: Public PDF
review_note: Inspected the report's validation design and headline results. The 2021 v200 product validation uses the CGLS-100 validation dataset updated to 2021 by revisiting a random subset and locations targeted for likely change. The report states global overall accuracy of 76.7% with a reported uncertainty of ±0.5 percentage points. The report is included as product-level context, not as a substitute for Fiji-specific assessment.
cautions: The global validation estimate is not directly comparable to a Fiji-domain estimate from the separate Fiji sample.
The WorldCover validation design and target population differ from the Fiji test sample.
Do not treat product-level global accuracy as evidence of local class accuracy.

issuer: John Duncan; Pacific Data Hub / Pacific Community
title: Fiji Land Use Land Cover Labels
identifier: Pacific Data Hub dataset page; modified 27 April 2023
edition: Related Fiji labelled-point dataset; operational class definitions
access_status: Public dataset documentation; ODbL
review_note: Inspected the public dataset description and class definitions. It documents cropland/agriculture as visible cropping or livestock-management activity, including recently fallow land with evidence of cropping or grazing; grassland as low vegetation without woody structure; scrubland as below-head-height vegetation with visible shrub/bush structure and no closed canopy; and trees as taller vegetation forming a clear canopy. It also describes manual interpretation using high-resolution basemaps with Planet and Sentinel-2 ancillary imagery and field verification for that related labelled dataset. These definitions are used here as supplementary evidence only: the repository has not proven that this companion dataset's full operational rubric was applied identically to every point in the separate 834-point Fiji test sample.
cautions: This is a related labelled-point dataset, not the 834-point test dataset itself; do not assume identical point-level labelling protocol without lineage evidence.
The documented Fiji visual definitions differ conceptually from WorldCover's LCCS cover thresholds; crosswalk decisions require explicit harmonisation.
ODbL applies; review attribution and share-alike obligations before redistributing substantial database contents.
